Wrong. There was NEVER a legitimate offer of a *sovereign* state, and Israel maintained a belligerent occupation over Gaza.

https://t.co/sbyFw1qxiP

https://t.co/YwMOuMDkoa

Camp David 2000 is the centrepiece of the rejection narrative. Ahron Bregman’s account, drawing on transcripts and participant records, shows that Ehud Barak moved further than any previous Israeli prime minister – on territory, on Jerusalem, on the willingness to countenance Palestinian sovereignty in parts of the Old City. However, the process was closer to forcing a reckoning than making peace. Patrick Tyler documents Barak’s strategy as an attempt to push Arafat into a final negotiation and, if he did not accept, declare that Israel had no partner. However, Arafat was not in a position to provide a definitive response either way. The Palestinians had wanted more months of preparatory talks, but Barak had not allowed it and had not implemented confidence-building commitments before the summit convened.

Early in the proceedings Barak killed the American written text, telling Bill Clinton “the paper no longer exists”, after which all discussions were oral with total deniability on anything proposed. Barak largely avoided substantive face-to-face negotiation with Arafat, saying he did not want Arafat to have a record, and thus preferred indirect channels through which positions could be floated and disowned. The summit then collapsed over Israeli sovereignty on the Haram al-Sharif, the Temple Mount compound containing the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa mosque. Barak would not relinquish it and Arafat could not concede it without Arab backing that had not been secured in advance, partly because Barak’s secrecy meant Arab leaders could not be briefed.

When Arafat asked for time to consult his leadership, Clinton treated the request less as a normal diplomatic step than as evasion, and the pressure shifted rapidly toward a yes-or-no reckoning that undermined the process.

Robert Malley co-authored with Hussein Agha a detailed rebuttal in the New York Review of Books arguing that the ‘generous offer’ framing was a post-hoc political construction. Malley was Clinton’s special assistant, directly involved in the talks, and Agha was a Palestinian academic with close ties to the Palestinian leadership and long involvement in back-channel diplomacy. Shlomo Ben-Ami, who was Israel’s chief negotiator, said in a 2006 Haaretz interview: “If I were a Palestinian, I would have rejected Camp David as well”. When the Israeli chief negotiator contradicts the rejection narrative, the narrative has a problem that more vivid memoir accounts cannot resolve.

The Clinton Parameters of December 2000 are a different matter, and the table’s failure to distinguish them from Camp David is one of its more significant distortions. The Parameters went further than Camp David on every core issue – including Palestinian sovereignty over the Haram – and represent the closest thing to an authoritative statehood framework. They were read orally rather than provided as a written document, because Barak feared Arafat would pocket any written text as an opening position, and Clinton wanted deniability should the proposals fail. On Bregman’s reading, Arafat’s failure to give the unambiguous ‘yes’ that Clinton demanded was a genuine missed opportunity, and Rashid later called it a strategic mistake. Shlaim’s interpretation complicates that verdict, observing that both sides responded with reservations. Israel’s own acceptance was heavily qualified by a twenty-page document, while Arafat’s qualified response was subsequently recast as outright rejection – partly, Clinton later told Saeb Erekat, the chief Palestinian negotiator, to preserve Barak’s domestic position. The failure was genuine, but the “Arafat rejected statehood” version of it is too simple.

Taba 2001

Taba in January 2001 appears in the table as another Palestinian rejection. Miguel Moratinos, the EU’s special envoy to the Middle East, produced a summary of where the parties stood at Taba, an unofficial document that became the main public record of the talks. The Clinton Parameters fed directly into Taba, hence why Taba was closer to agreement than at any previous point, with the parties’ own closing statement saying they had never been closer. Taba collapsed under a dying mandate: Barak was days from an election he was expected to lose, the talks had no durable political backing, and any understanding reached there would almost certainly have depended on a Barak Government that was about to disappear. Taba ended on 27 January, nine days before Sharon won the election on 6 February. There would be no serious negotiations for another seven years.

2008

The Ehud Olmert entry requires the most imaginative reading of the word ‘rejection’. Months of talks culminated in a September 2008 meeting at which Olmert showed Mahmoud Abbas a map but would not leave it with him. Abbas asked to study it and consult his team – the response any negotiator would give before formally responding to a complex territorial proposal – and Olmert refused. Abbas said he would return with his negotiators for formal talks, but Olmert resigned weeks later under corruption investigations and the Netanyahu Government that followed repudiated the Olmert framework. Olmert himself has said publicly that Abbas did not reject the proposal but asked for time to consult.

The fair criticism of Abbas is that he neither responded with a counter-proposal nor made any effort to put Olmert’s offer on the record before the Olmert Government collapsed, thus leaving the most serious proposal he had received to disappear with the administration that made it. Although that is a legitimate failure of Palestinian diplomacy, it is not the same as rejecting a signed, written, implementable statehood agreement.

So, at the decisive moments in 2000, 2001, and 2008, there was no formal written Israeli proposal with agreed maps that Palestinians could have signed or refused. Positions were advanced orally, incrementally, and with deniability built in. The ‘generous offer’ narrative depends on that absence of a written record, so that subsequent recharacterisation of what was actually proposed could not be checked.

Billionaire and bear shifter Kort Behrens has been lucky in business but unlucky in love—after two failed marriages and a string of gold diggers, he’s given up hope of finding a real connection. Elizabeth Murphy, a widow for four years, has rebuilt her life through her Reiki practice and the quiet companionship of her cat, Puzzle, still carrying the quiet ache of a long marriage that never fully satisfied her deeper desires. Will they seize this second chance at a happily-ever-after, or will doubts and fears snatch it away? On Gambler’s Folly, every love story is a gamble—and Fate always deals the final hand. text:
💔 STILL SEEKING ANSWERS: THE MURDER OF CHERYL RIVERA 🔍
Nearly three decades later, Cheryl Rivera’s family is still waiting for answers.
On August 25, 1995, shortly before the evening rush hour, children walking through a wooded area behind the Liberty Shopping Center in Randallstown, Maryland, made a heartbreaking discovery: the badly decomposed body of a woman.
Through dental records, she was identified as 30-year-old Cheryl Rivera, a mother of four. 
An autopsy determined that Cheryl had been strangled, and her death was ruled a homicide.
Cheryl had last been seen alive nearly a month earlier, on July 27, 1995, after leaving a party on Cinnamon Circle in Randallstown.
Despite an investigation, the case eventually went cold. Limited evidence and the secluded location where Cheryl was found made finding answers difficult.
But cold cases are never truly forgotten.
Today, investigators are still hoping someone remembers something they saw, heard, or experienced that night. Maybe someone attended that party. Maybe someone saw Cheryl afterward. Maybe there is a detail that seemed insignificant at the time but could be important today.
🔎 Technology has advanced. Memories can resurface. New witnesses can come forward. And answers are still possible.
A cash reward of up to $2,000 is being offered for information that leads to progress in Cheryl’s case.
Cheryl's family deserves answers, and her case deserves to be remembered.
If you know something, even if you aren't sure it matters please consider coming forward.

I turn 50 today...
Chamath Palihapitiya
Sep 03, 2026
I turn 50 today. This is a message to my kids but I offer it to you in case any of it rings useful…

I was born in Sri Lanka in 1976 in a country that, at the time, was about to enter a decades long civil war. My father was able to get stationed at the Sri Lankan High Commission in Canada for four years in the early 80s - when some of the fighting was most severe - and which from our vantage point in Canada gave us some respite from an otherwise omnipresent conflict.

He came as a diplomat but then my father filed for refugee status after four years when his life was threatened by militants. We stayed in Canada as refugees. My dad never really landed on his feet and we grew up on welfare.

My mom stepped up. She did an incredible thing and put our family on her back and kept marching forward. Sometimes the steps were very small but she always tried to keep moving forward.

I worked at Burger King starting at 14, giving my paycheck to my mom and dad to support our family in the role that I was assigned - earn enough to pay for our bus passes because we couldn’t afford a car.

I was a loser growing up. Some friends, some good memories but mostly forgettable and lonely. I wasn’t very studious but did get my act together in my final year and got into a great university.

I immigrated to the US soon after graduating and found an opportunity. Things clicked and I have been traveling a path to find myself ever since. Only in America is this possible…

I worked hard, followed the rules, paid my taxes and stayed in California out of loyalty for the opportunities it has given me despite its dysfunction.

I found my wife here. Had my kids here. Found my tribe here.

There have been some very hard times as well - deaths, divorce, financial pain, mistakes of omission and mistakes of commission. You can’t dwell on these things - they are weights that will pull you down if you’re not careful. Learn from them. Respect them. BUT MOVE ON.

To think 50 years ago I could have ever gotten a chance to meet the people I’ve met and have had the experiences I’ve had would have been mind boggling to my parents. It’s mind boggling to me now.

We forget often and try to convince others it’s not true but America truly is the best country in the world. Everything and anything is possible here. I can testify. Be grateful to be here.

This is the only place that gives EVERYONE a chance to live a great adventure. The first 50 years have been that for me - an incredible adventure.

Notice there is nothing here about accomplishments or money. Because it doesn’t matter and it won’t matter.

You will be dust in less than 100 years from now and the decision to be remembered won’t be yours so stop sweating it. It’s not in your control.

So what is in your control?

Be kind. Have fun. Work on something meaningful to you. Find your tribe. Try to find perspective. Find an incredible partner. Have a bunch of kids. Live an adventure. Forgive your parents - they were doing the best they could even if that wasn’t what you deserved.

I will do what I can to make my next 50 years a wild ride.

You should too.

I love you and thank you. ❤️

Traders are betting 3% that streamer ArrowCS will eat a bug live on air before the end of the year. But the key here isn't even the bet, but the rules. The bug can be alive, dead, cooked, or raw. The streamer must put it in their mouth and close their lips completely. An insect protein bar doesn't count. The legal framework is so detailed, it's as if an international contract is at stake, not someone else's dinner.

Another 13% is betting that professional CS2 player ropz will be stopped by the police again in 2026. Some are studying his matches, others his team uniform, and still others, apparently, are monitoring traffic conditions along the route.

Meanwhile, Kim Kardashian has a 7% interest on an announcement about successfully passing the California bar exam by the end of 2027. Trading volume is currently only $308, but there's already a small group of people whose financial future depends on her study schedule.

And a full-fledged prison sentence market has developed around blogger Jack Doherty. 92% of offers are for no prison time, 8% for less than two years, and 2% for five years or more. The total volume is already approaching $23,000. Apparently, court documents are now part of the content analyst's mandatory toolkit.

@Polymarket continues to prove that anything can have a price.

text:
Below is the full transcription of the anti-Zionist petition (titled "A Statement to the Peace Conference") presented to @potus President Woodrow Wilson on March 4, 1919, by a committee of prominent American Jews, for transmission to the Paris Peace Conference. This document, originally published in The New York Times on March 5, 1919, under the headline "PROTEST TO WILSON AGAINST ZIONIST STATE," articulates objections to the establishment of a Jewish national home or state in Palestine, emphasizing democratic principles, Jewish integration, and opposition to political segregation based on race or religion. 
https://t.co/X5BaObGyo8
 As you noted, Dr. Roy, its arguments—rooted in historical emancipation, rejection of nationalism, and calls for equal rights irrespective of creed—remain highly relevant to ongoing debates on Zionism, statehood, and international norms in the Israel-Palestine context.
Full Text of the Petition
"As a future form of government for Palestine will undoubtedly be considered by the approaching Peace Conference, we, the undersigned citizens of the United States, unite in this statement, setting forth our objections to the organization of a Jewish State in Palestine as proposed by the Zionist Societies in this country and Europe and to the segregation of the Jews as a nationalistic unit in any country. We feel that in so doing we are voicing the opinion of the majority of American Jews born in this country and of those foreign-born who have lived here long enough to thoroughly assimilate American political and social conditions. The American Zionists represent, according to the most recent statistics available, only a small proportion of the Jews living in this country, about 150,000 out of 3,500,000, (American Jewish Year Book, 1918, Philadelphia.) At the outset we wish to indicate our entire sympathy with the efforts of Zionists which aim to secure for Jews at present living in lands of oppression a refuge in Palestine or elsewhere, where they may freely develop their capabilities and carry on their activities as free citizens.
But we raise our voices in warning and protest against the demand of the Zionists for the reorganization of the Jews as a national unit to whom, now or in the future, territorial sovereignty in Palestine shall be committed. This demand not only misinterprets the trend of the history of the Jews, who ceased to be a nation 2,000 years ago, but involves the limitation and possible annulment of the larger claims of Jews for full citizenship and human rights in all lands in which those rights are not yet secure. For the very reason that the new era upon which the world is entering aims to establish government everywhere on principles of true democracy, we reject the Zionistic project of a 'national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.'
Zionism arose as a result of the intolerable conditions under which Jews have been forced to live in Russia and Rumania. But it is evident that for the Jewish population of these countries, variously estimated at from 6,000,000 to 10,000,000, Palestine can become no homeland. Even with the improvement of neglected conditions of this country, its limited area can offer no solution. The Jewish question in Russia and Rumania can be settled only within those countries by the grant of full rights of citizenship to Jews.
We are all the more opposed to the Zionists, because they themselves distinctly repudiate the solely ameliorative program. They demand and hail with delight the Balfour Declaration establish 'a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine,' i. e., a home not merely for Jews living in countries in which they are oppressed, but for Jews universally. No Jew, wherever he may live, can consider himself free from the implications of such a grant.
The willingness of Jews interested in the welfare of their brethren to aid in redeeming Palestine from the blight of centuries of Turkish misrule is no acceptance of the Zionist project to segregate Jews as a political unit and to reinstitute a section of such a political unit in Palestine or elsewhere. At the present juncture in the world's affairs, when lands that have hitherto been subjected to foreign domination are to be recognized as free and independent States, we rejoice in the avowed proposal of the Peace Congress to put into practical application the fundamental principles of democracy. That principle, which asserts equal rights for all citizens of a State irrespective of creed or ethnic descent, should be applied in such a manner as to exclude segregation of any kind, be it nationalistic or other. Such segregation must inevitably create differences among the sections of the population of a country. Any such plan of segregation is necessarily reactionary in its tendency, undemocratic in spirit and totally contrary to the practices of free government, especially as these are exemplified by our own country. We therefore strongly urge the abandonment of such a basis for the reorganization of any State.
Against such a political segregation of the Jews in Palestine or elsewhere we object.
Because the Jews are dedicated, heart and soul, to the welfare of the countries in which they dwell under free conditions. All Jews repudiate every suspicion of a double allegiance, but to our minds it is necessarily implied in, and cannot by any logic be eliminated from, the establishment of a sovereign state for the Jews in Palestine.
By the large part taken by them in the great war the Jews have once and for all shattered the base aspersions of the anti-Semites which charged them with being aliens in every land, incapable of true patriotism and prompted only by sinister and self-seeking motives. Moreover, it is safe to assume that the overwhelming bulk of the Jews of America, England, France, Italy, Holland, Switzerland, and the other lands of freedom have no thought whatever of surrendering their citizenship in these lands in order to resort to a 'Jewish homeland in Palestine.' As a rule those who favor such a restoration advocate it not for themselves, but for others. Those who act thus, and yet insist on their patriotic attachment to the countries of which they are citizens, are self-deceived in their profession of Zionism and under the spell of an emotional romanticism or of a religious sentiment fostered through centuries of gloom.
We also object to political segregation of Jews for those who take their Zionistic professions seriously as referring not to others, but to themselves. Granted that the establishment of a sovereign Jewish State in Palestine would lead many to emigrate to that land, the political conditions of the millions who would be unable to migrate for generations to come, if ever, would be made far more precarious. Rumania-despite the pledges of the Berlin treaty-has legally branded her Jews as aliens, though many are descended from families settled in that country longer than the present Rumanian Government has existed. The establishment of a Jewish state will manifestly serve the more violent rulers of that and other lands as a new justification for additional repressive legislation. The multitudes who remain would be subject to worse perils, if possible, even though the few who escape might prosper in Palestine.
We object to the political segregation also of those who might succeed in establishing themselves in Palestine. The proposition involves dangers which, it is manifest, have not had the serious consideration of those who are so zealous in its advocacy. These dangers are adverted to in a most kindly spirit of warning by Sir George Adam Smith, who is generally acknowledged to be the greatest authority in the world on everything connected with Palestine either past or present.
In a recent publication, Syria and the Holy Land,' he points out that there is absolutely no fixity to the boundaries of Palestine. These have varied greatly in the course of the centuries. The claims to various sections of this undefined territory would unquestionably evoke bitter controversies. It is not true,' says Sir George, that Palestine is the national home of the Jewish people, and of no other people.' It is not correct to call its non-Jewish inhabitants Arabs' or to say that they have left no image of their spirit and made no history except in the Great Mosque.' Nor can we evade the fact that Christian communities have been as long in possession of their portion of this land as ever the Jews were. These are legitimate questions,' he says, stirred up by the claims of Zionism, but the Zionists have not yet fully faced them.
To subject the Jews to the possible recurrence of such bitter and sanguinary conflicts, which would be inevitable, would be a crime against the triumph of their whole past history and against the lofty and world embracing visions of their great prophets and leaders.
Though these grave difficulties may be met, still we protest against the political segregation of the Jews and the re-establishment in Palestine of a distinctively Jewish State as utterly opposed to the principles of democracy which it is the avowed purpose of the world's Peace Conference to establish.
Contrary to Democratic Ideals.
Whether the Jews be regarded as a race or as a religion,' it is contrary to democratic principles for which the world war was waged to found a nation on either or both of these bases. America, England, France, Italy, Switzerland, and all the most advanced nations of the world are composed of representatives of many races and religions. Their glory lies in the freedom of conscience and worship, in the liberty of thought and custom which binds the followers of many faiths and varied civilizations in the common bonds of political union. A Jewish State involves fundamental limitations as to race and religion, else the term 'Jewish' means nothing. To unite Church and State, in any form, as under the old Jewish hierarchy, would be a leap backward of 2,000 years.
The rights of other creeds and races will be respected under Jewish dominance,' is the assurance of Zionism, but the keynotes of democracy are neither condescension nor tolerance, but justice and equality. All this applies with special force to a country like Palestine. That land is filled with associations sacred to the followers of three great religions and as a result of migrating movements of many countries contains an extraordinary number of different ethnic groups, far out of proportion to the small extent of the country itself. Such a condition points clearly to a reorganization of Palestine on the broadest possible basis.
We object to the political segregation of the Jews because it is an error to assume that the bond uniting them is of a national character. They are bound by two factors: First. The bond of common religious beliefs and aspirations; and, secondly, the bond of common traditions, customs, and experiences, largely, alas, of common trials and sufferings. Nothing in their present status suggests that they form in any real sense a separate nationalistic unit. The reorganization of Palestine, as far as it affects the Jews, is but part of a far larger issue, namely, the constructive endeavor to secure the emancipation of the Jews in all the lands in which they dwell. This movement, inaugurated in the eighteenth century and advancing with steady progress through the western lands, was checked by such reactionary tendencies as caused the expulsion of the Poles from Eastern Prussia and the massacre of Armenians in Turkey. As directed against Jews, these tendencies crystallized into a political movement called anti-Semitism, which had its rise in Germany. Its virulence spread (especially) throughout Eastern Europe and led to cruel outbreaks in Rumania and elsewhere and to the pogroms of Russia, with their dire consequences.
To guard against such evils in the future we urge that the great constructive movement, so sadly interrupted, be reinstituted, and that efficient measures be taken to insure the protection of the law and the full rights of citizenship to Jews in every land. If the basis of the reorganization of Governments is henceforth to be democratic, it cannot be contemplated to exclude any group of people from the enjoyment of full rights.
As to the future of Palestine, it is our fervent hope that what was once a 'promised land' for the Jews may become a 'land of promise' for all races and creeds, safeguarded by the League of Nations which, it is expected, will be one of the fruits of the Peace Conference to whose deliberations the world now looks forward so anxiously and so full of hope. We ask that Palestine be constituted as a free and independent state, to be governed under a democratic form of government, recognizing no distinctions of creed or race or ethnic descent, and with adequate power to protect the country against oppression of any kind. We do not wish to see Palestine, either now or at any time in the future, organized as a Jewish State."

text:
Harland Sanders is six years old in 1896 when his father dies, leaving him to cook for his younger siblings while his mother works long shifts in Henryville, Indiana.

By seventh grade, he drops out of school for good. His teenage years drift through jobs: farmhand, streetcar conductor, soldier. At 16, he lies about his age to join the Army.

Almost nothing works out in his twenties and thirties. Insurance sales fails. A ferry company fails. Law, studied by mail order, doesn't stick either.

Then, in 1930, he opens a service station along a busy Kentucky highway near Corbin. To bring in extra money, he starts cooking meals for travelers who stop for gas.

His chicken becomes the reason people stop.

By 1940, Sanders has perfected his recipe: a blend of eleven herbs and spices, cooked fast under pressure so the outside stays crisp and the inside stays juicy. His roadside spot grows into a full restaurant and motel.

Here's what makes it worse: none of it protects him from what's coming.

In the 1950s, a new interstate routes traffic around Corbin entirely. His customers disappear almost overnight, and he has to sell the restaurant just to cover his debts.

At 65, an age when most people are winding down, Sanders is starting over with a recipe, a car, and not much else.

His first Social Security check arrives for $105. He later says it felt like the government telling him he couldn't take care of himself. That isn't the ending he wants.

So he loads his car with a pressure cooker and his spice mix, and starts driving from restaurant to restaurant, cooking his chicken for owners on the spot. If they like it, he offers a deal: a few cents for every piece sold, in exchange for using his recipe.

Most say no. Some don't even let him finish cooking. In his first two years on the road, he signs up only five restaurants willing to try it.

He keeps driving anyway.

In 1952, restaurant owner Pete Harman in South Salt Lake City, Utah, agrees to give it a shot. Harman's sales triple. A sign painter working for Harman coins a name for the dish: Kentucky Fried Chicken.

That single yes changes everything.

Word travels between restaurant owners, and handshake deals multiply. By 1964, there are roughly 600 Kentucky Fried Chicken franchises, all built on a recipe cooked up by a man who refused to stay retired.

That same year, at 73, Sanders sells the U.S. side of the business for $2 million. He keeps traveling anyway, now as the company's face, touring restaurants in his white suit and black tie for the rest of his life.

He dies in 1980 at 90. His personal fortune is estimated at $3.5 million, modest next to the empire built on his name.

Today, KFC operates more than 31,000 restaurants in roughly 150 countries, all tracing back to a highway service station and a recipe finalized in 1940.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

The most dangerous man is not the one who wins a battle. It is the one who cannot be absorbed after he loses.

On September 5, 1877, at Fort Robinson, Nebraska, the Army tried to absorb Crazy Horse.

A year earlier he had helped break Custer on the Little Bighorn. Winter, hunger, and Colonel Nelson Miles did what the Seventh Cavalry could not. On May 6 he rode in with nearly nine hundred of his people and some two thousand ponies, laid down his rifles, and offered his left hand—the side of the heart—and said he wanted the peace to last. That should have ended it. It did not. Power hates a man it cannot use. Other Lakota chiefs who had already surrendered watched the attention he received and felt envy, that quiet acid that does more work than armies. A scout’s mistranslation of a remark about fighting the Nez Perce became rumor. Rumor became an order: confine him. Ship him. Break the name by putting it in a room.

He came that afternoon in a striped cotton shirt, deer-hide leggings, beaded moccasins, a red blanket. No paint. No war shirt. He was walked toward the guardhouse. Then he saw the cells—or smelled them. Chained men. A stink of men who did not leave. In that second the last illusion died. A warrior who has never signed a paper and never sat for a camera understands instantly what a cage is. It is not a building. It is the death of the self while the body is still breathing.

He whirled.

Little Big Man, once a companion, now wearing the metal of the agency police, leapt on his back. Crazy Horse freed an arm and slashed him across the wrist. Captain Kennington shouted not to shoot. One shot and the packed ground would have become a second war. Private William Gentles, forty-seven years old, 14th Infantry, drove an eighteen-inch bayonet into his side. One thrust, perhaps two. The blade passed through both kidneys and stopped half an inch from coming out the other side. A second lunge missed and stuck in the pine of the doorframe.

“Let me go, my friend—you have hurt me plenty bad.” Then the sentence that ends every campaign against an ungovernable man: “He has killed me now.”

They would not let him die in the cell. Touch the Clouds blocked the door. Dr. Valentine McGillycuddy found him on the floor of the adjutant’s office, on his back, grinding his teeth, frothing, pulse skipping beats. Morphine. His father Worm spoke. Crazy Horse answered that it was no good for the people to depend on him any longer. He died around midnight.

Seventeen witnesses. Seventeen stories. Accident. His own knife. A soldier’s deliberate lunge. Official telegrams written in fog. The fog is the point. When a system cannot own a man, it must make his death look like a scuffle.

Touch the Clouds laid a hand on the still chest and said it was good. He had looked for death, and it had come.

Learn the law. First starve him. Then surround him with rivals. Then walk him toward a room that smells of chains. If he recognizes the room, you have only one tool left. Some men can be flattered. Some can be bought. A few cannot be confined. History does not debate those men. It waits for the doorway.

America 250 🇺🇸

text:
Building anything new comes with a hard truth, you will never wake up one day and feel completely ready.

Waiting for 100 percent certainty is just fear dressed up as preparation, You end up trapped in the planning loop.

• Reading another stack of case studies to avoid making a cold call.
• Watching endless tutorials instead of writing the first line of code.
• Tweaking a pitch deck for the tenth time rather than sending it to an investor.
• Polishing a landing page when nobody has even seen the prototype yet.

Research shows that elite performers do not wait to feel confident before they start, Reid Hoffman, the founder of LinkedIn, famously noted that if you are not embarrassed by the first version of your product, you launched too late. 

Amazon operates on a rule where leaders make decisions with about 70 percent of the information they wish they had, If you wait for 90 percent, you are moving too slow.

The real trap is thinking you can think your way into clarity, It rarely works like that.

Action creates the data you actually need

A live post gives you real engagement metrics, while a draft in your notes gives you zero.

A basic product in the wild reveals what customers will actually pay for, not what they say they like.

An open trade forces you to manage real risk instead of running safe simulations on paper.

A quick experiment exposes the blind spots that no amount of reading could ever predict.

Action produces the feedback, The feedback produces the clarity.

Hit publish. Put the offer out. Test the idea. 

I am still reminding myself of this every day, but the only way forward is to push the button and see what happens.

Was Blondie's Debbie Harry really abducted by Ted Bundy?
Thomas Leatham
TUE 11TH OCT 2022 16.00 BST
There are several urban myths surrounding the lives of famous musicians. Take, for instance, the claims that Keith Richards snorted his father’s remains or that the first Kiss comic book is infused with the band members’ blood. There is also the claim that Debbie Harry of Blondie was once abducted by the notorious serial killer Ted Bundy.

Of the subject, Harry once explained: “I was trying to get a cab on the lower east side of the Village in New York, and it was kind of late. This was back in the early 1970s. I wasn’t even in a band then. I was trying to get across town to an after-hours club. A little white car pulls up, and the guy offers me a ride. So I just continued to try to flag a cab down. But he was very persistent, and he asked where I was going. It was only a couple of blocks away, and he said, ‘Well, I’ll give you a ride.'”

She added: “I got in the car, and it was summertime, and the windows were all rolled up except about an inch and a half at the top. So I was sitting there, and he wasn’t really talking to me. Automatically, I sort of reached to roll down the window and realized there was no door handle, no window crank, no nothing. The inside of the car was totally stripped out.”

Regardless of the mysterious person, it must have been a frightening experience for a young Harry. Getting into a car with a stranger who had no escape route immediately spells out trouble. Upon reflection, in later years, Harry felt adamant that the man was Bundy. She continued: “I got very nervous. I reached my arm out through the little crack and stretched down, and opened the car from the outside. As soon as he saw that, he tried to turn the corner really fast, and I spun out of the car and landed in the middle of the street.”

Detailing the incident further, Harry added: “It was right after his execution that I read about him. I hadn’t thought about that incident in years. The whole description of how he operated and what he looked like and the kind of car he drove and the time frame he was doing that in that area of the country fit exactly. I said, ‘My God, it was him.'”

However, many people have argued that Harry’s account does not match up with the other reports of Bundy’s whereabouts. Bundy was not known to have been in New York City in the early 1970s, nor was he said to have started abducting women until 1974. The fact that Harry says she wasn’t in a band at the time suggests that her story took place no later than 1973, a time in which she joined the Stilettos.

Bundy was also not known to have driven a “stripped out” vehicle without door handles and window levers. How and to whom did Jesus pay our ransom?
Answer
A ransom is something that is paid to provide for the release of someone who is held captive. Jesus paid our ransom to free us from sin, death, and hell. Throughout the books of Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy are found God’s requirements for sacrifices. In Old Testament times, God commanded the Israelites to make animal sacrifices for substitutionary atonement; that is, an animal’s death took the place of a person’s death, death being the penalty for sin (Romans 6:23). Exodus 29:36a states, "Each day you must sacrifice a young bull as an offering for the atonement of sin."

God demands holiness (1 Peter 1:15-16). God’s Law demands holiness. We cannot give God full holiness because of the sins we commit (Romans 3:23); therefore, God demands satisfaction of His Law. Sacrifices to Him satisfied the requirements. This is where Jesus comes in. Hebrews 9:12-15 tells us: "Once for all time he took blood into that Most Holy Place, but not the blood of goats and calves. He took his own blood, and with it he secured our salvation forever. Under the old system, the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a young cow could cleanse people’s bodies from ritual defilement. Just think how much more the blood of Christ will purify our hearts from deeds that lead to death so that we can worship the living God. For by the power of the eternal Spirit, Christ offered himself to God as a perfect sacrifice for our sins. That is why he is the one who mediates the new covenant between God and people, so that all who are invited can receive the eternal inheritance God has promised them. For Christ died to set them free from the penalty of the sins they had committed under that first covenant."

Also, read Romans 8:3-4, "The law of Moses could not save us, because of our sinful nature. But God put into effect a different plan to save us. He sent his own Son in a human body like ours, except that ours are sinful. God destroyed sin’s control over us by giving his Son as a sacrifice for our sins. He did this so that the requirement of the law would be fully accomplished for us who no longer follow our sinful nature but instead follow the Spirit."

Clearly, Jesus paid the ransom for our lives to God. That ransom was His own life, the shedding of His own blood, a sacrifice. Due to His sacrificial death, each person on earth has the opportunity to accept that gift of atonement and be forgiven by God. For without His death, God’s Law would still need to be satisfied—by our own death.

ｇ、分かった日本語で喧嘩しよう・・・
ピンチョン作品のグノーシス論を、主要な研究とテクストに沿って確認します。Pynchon never writes a treatise on second-century heresy. He uses Gnostic cosmology as a machine for thinking about power: a false world built by rulers who are not God, a spark of real knowledge trapped inside it, and the near-impossibility of getting out without becoming what you fight.

The standard map, set by Harold Bloom and Dwight Eddins’s The Gnostic Pynchon (1990), looks like this.
Gnostic termIn PynchonDemiurgeThey; the System; the Rocket-cartel; capital that pretends it is natureArchonsBureaucrats, cartels, Pavlovians, IG Farben, the postal monopoly, later the internet and the war on drugsKenoma (empty world)The Zone after the Reich; suburban California; any landscape where meaning is administeredPleromaGlimpsed only as rumor, song, or light that does not stayDivine sparkPreterite bodies, jazz, waste, the unchosenGnosisParanoia that sometimes sees truly, and sometimes only multiplies cages
The catch, which later critics insist on, is that Pynchon puts Gnosticism on both sides. The System is gnostic in Eric Voegelin’s secular sense: an elite that claims secret knowledge and remakes the world as a prison. The Counterforce is gnostic in the older heretical sense: sparks trying to wake up inside that prison. He trusts neither version all the way.
The cosmology he keeps recycling
Ancient Gnostic myth, especially Sethian and Valentinian versions, says the visible cosmos is a botched construction. A lesser craftsman, the Demiurge, often identified with the Old Testament creator, builds matter as a trap. Planetary archons staff the checkpoints. A fragment of alien light is sealed in human bodies. Salvation is not faith or works but gnosis: knowing where you are and who built the walls.
Pynchon secularizes the myth without discarding its heat. Technology, war, and information replace the seven heavens. The rocket in Gravity’s Rainbow is the clearest demiurgic object: a parabola that looks like destiny, built by men who talk like priests. They do not merely use the world. They claim to have authored its laws.
Calvinism, which he inherited from New England ancestors, rhymes with this. Elect and preterite are a Protestant version of saved sparks and leftover matter. Pynchon keeps the preterite and throws away the comfort of election. The discarded are his moral center. The elect look like archons.
Novel by novel
V. (1963)
History stiffens into inanimate plot. The Lady V. is less a woman than a principle of the made thing replacing the living thing. Already the suspicion: someone is assembling the century as an artifact. Stencil hunts a pattern; Profane stumbles through waste. Neither gets out.
The Crying of Lot 49 (1966)
Oedipa Maas is the most Gnostic protagonist in miniature. A revelation arrives as waste-systems, muted post horns, the Tristero. The Scurvhamites in the invented play history are explicit: a Calvinist sect sliding into the gnostic heresy that Creation is a machine, one half moved by God, the other by a soulless automatic anti-God. Tristero can be read as that Other. The novel refuses to say whether Oedipa has seen the archons or invented them. Gnosis here is formally identical to paranoia. That identity is the point.
Gravity’s Rainbow (1973)
This is the Gnostic epic.
They / the Firm / the Rocket-cartel occupy the archon slot. Charles Hohmann and others map Them directly onto planetary rulers who keep souls from leaving matter.
Blicero’s firing of rocket 00000, with Gottfried inside, is a rite of transcendence-through-death. Eddins reads it as gnostic mysticism that “incorporates life into a larger death”: escape from earth purchased by sacrificing a body to the machine.
Slothrop’s scattering is the opposite rite. The self dissolves back into the Zone instead of ascending. Critics argue whether that is Orphic return to earth or failed gnosis.
Father Rapier’s sermon splits They from we: as long as we know They can kill us, They win; resistance makes their power decay. That is political Gnosticism, not church doctrine.
The book plants a fake Gospel of Thomas fragment as a chapter epigraph (“Dear Mom, I put a couple of people in hell today”). Joshua Pederson argues Pynchon is blocking end-times reading: like the real Gospel of Thomas, Gravity’s Rainbow will not deliver a clean apocalypse. The rocket looks eschatological. The novel will not let the ending be Last Judgment.
Bloom’s formula is still the sharpest: in Pynchon you can achieve gnosis and pay for it with impotence. Knowledge of the System does not confer the power to leave it.

Vineland (1990)
The archons become the Nixon–Reagan security state and the culture industry. Frenesi’s betrayal is a spark collaborating with the prison. The Tube is a cheap pleroma. Animism and family stubbornness do more work than secret knowledge. Gnosticism is still there as the shape of Control, less as a path out.

Mason & Dixon (1997)
The Line is a demiurgic inscription on living land. Surveying is how archons write. The novel’s tenderness toward unmapped space, talking dogs, and the preterite on both sides of the Line is anti-gnostic in Eddins’s Orphic sense: earth is not a mistake.

Against the Day (2006)
The myth comes back as comedy and as monastery.

Early Pynchon criticism found “Gnostic fatalism.” Ron S. Judy and others read this book as Gnostic comedy: the same Manichaean war of Elect and Preterite, technology and spirit, but with more room for farce, anarchist plot, and actual withdrawal.

Cyprian Latewood ends in a Bogomil–Orphic monastery in Thrace, a historically Gnostic-adjacent dualist sect. He offers himself to Night. The scene gathers Shekhinah, Manichaean light/dark, Orphic descent, and a refusal of the rocket’s phallic gnosis. Whether that retreat is resistance or another form of Control is left unstable—which is Pynchon’s habit. Kathryn Hume hears a Catholic tonality. Other readers hear syncretism hiding non-Christian cosmology inside Christian camouflage. Both can be true because Pynchon likes double doors.

Later books
Inherent Vice and Bleeding Edge keep the archon structure (LAPD, internet, 9/11 security) and shrink gnosis to a private weather: you glimpse the wiring, then the fog closes. The spark does not found a church.

The argument among critics
Eddins, drawing on Hans Jonas and Voegelin, set the terms: Pynchon is on a religious quest for organic order against two false exits, total chaos and total control. He contrasts gnostic mysticism (life swallowed by death, the rocket) with Orphic naturalism (death folded back into earth). On this view Pynchon is finally anti-gnostic. He hates the System’s claim to secret law, and he also distrusts the mystic who wants to leave matter behind.

Revisionists say Eddins imported Voegelin’s Cold War use of “gnostic” (progressivism, totalitarianism as mass gnostic movements) and missed the ancient Gnostics’ hatred of power. Jeffrey Lamar Howard treats Pynchon, with Dick and Nabokov, as embracing the heresy: the Counterforce are gnostic rebels against an archontic technocratic elite. The novel names heretics and Gnostics among those who oppose the Rocket-cartel.
A third line, Richard Moss’s “preterite theology,” refuses to pick. Oppression speaks Calvinist election and gnostic Control. Resistance speaks animism, Zen, and a feminized or earthly gnosis. The books are a workshop of heterodox fragments, not a church.

That third line fits the fiction best. Pynchon is not a Sethian. He is a collagist of condemned cosmologies.
What he keeps and what he will not grant

He keeps:
the intuition that the official world is a construction
the moral privilege of those the construction discards
the comedy and terror of trying to read the construction from inside it
light that is real and does not belong to Them

He will not grant:

a clean exit
a priesthood of the knowing

contempt for bodies, sex, waste, or the planet
an ending in which gnosis becomes government

That last refusal is why he is not Philip K. Dick. Dick often wants the veil to drop. Pynchon lets the veil thicken as you stare. Oedipa at the auction, Slothrop scattered, the Chums of Chance sailing off the map: knowledge arrives as a loss of position.
If you want a single sentence: in Pynchon, Gnosticism is the true shape of modern power and a compromised name for the wish to wake from it. The Demiurge has incorporated. The spark is still in the dump. Neither fact produces salvation. Both keep the books from collapsing into either cynicism or sermon.

Why are people who should still be learning being pushed into becoming teachers and commentators? Allow people to develop before constructing platforms around their opinions.

The treatment of Muslim blood is even uglier. People who have never smelled a battlefield speak casually about populations who watched their homes disappear and buried relatives with their own hands. Syria becomes content. Bosnia becomes an argument. Palestine becomes engagement. Sudan becomes another debate. The victims themselves sometimes receive less attention than personalities arguing about what supposedly happened to them.

When people who actually lived through these events offer correction or sincere advice privately, only to watch the opposite position performed publicly, Muslims should possess enough discernment to recognise what they are watching. Truth does not become less true because it performs badly with an audience.

Then you hear Bosnia dismissed as though it were not a real country, while Muslims who speak about Muslim unity, security and strength are caricatured as “head choppers”. Personalities disappear following their own controversies, later resurface, and somehow find themselves welcomed onto platforms belonging to people who spend the rest of their time lecturing Muslims about morality and accountability.

The hypocrisy writes itself.

But Muslims cannot blame the algorithm for everything. The algorithm supplies what audiences reward. Every time Muslims elevate an unqualified personality because he is entertaining, circulate inflammatory clips without verification, defend celebrities as though criticism of them were criticism of Islam, or mistake visibility for authority, they help manufacture the circus they later complain about.

Muslim youth especially need to wake up to something far more serious than internet drama: you are deciding who helps shape your understanding of Allah جل جلاله, His religion and the world around you. Someone making you laugh, sounding confident or humiliating an opponent on a livestream tells you absolutely nothing about whether he is qualified to teach you.

text:
What We Become Together

Sodium is an unstable metal that can explode in water.

Chlorine is a poisonous gas.

Together they become table salt.

Pretty ridiculous.

Two individually alarming things meet and become something I sprinkle on my eggs.

Neither sodium nor chlorine is salty.

Saltiness exists only after they form a bond.

It is an emergent property.

Maybe... people work this way too.

Maybe sometimes we don’t fall in love only with another person.

Maybe we fall in love with who we become around them.

I’ve known people who made me funny.
Not made me laugh. Made me funny.

Some people drew out the nerd.
Some the theater kid.
Some the competitor.

Some brought out this unbearably sweet, childlike creature who apparently lived inside me running barefoot throwing heart confetti everywhere.

Others introduced me to less charming residents.

The timid one.
The codependent one.
The cold one.
The angry one.

I have met a lot of myself through other people.

Eventually I got curious about all these women.

So I climbed down into a Murakami-style psychological well and sat with them.

It was dark as fuck down there.

One was crying.
One was furious.
One was laughing hysterically.

Attachment theory says our earliest relationships teach our nervous systems what intimacy feels like.

It recognizes something familiar and goes:
OH! LOVE! I KNOW THIS ONE!

Meanwhile the conscious mind is screaming:
THAT IS CLEARLY AN EMOTIONAL HAZARD.

This may be why certain relationship patterns repeat.

We unconsciously draw people toward us who illuminate the parts of ourselves that need healing.

Patterns perpetuate themselves until something interrupts them.

Sometimes that something is awareness.
Sometimes therapy.
Sometimes exhaustion.

Sometimes you simply wake up one morning and think:

Actually, fuck this.

Enlightenment comes in many forms.

We like to imagine ourselves as independent objects.

I am me.
You are you.

We meet.
We separate.

Back to factory settings.

Except... there are no factory settings.

A phrase someone used becomes part of your vocabulary.

Someone introduces you to music you still listen to twenty years later.

Someone loves you in a way that teaches you something.

Someone hurts you in a way that teaches you something you desperately wish had been optional.

People leave.

But they leave fingerprints.

And we leave fingerprints too.

That’s why I have trouble calling even some of my worst relationships mistakes.

I don’t mean the suffering was necessary.

But it happened 🤷🏻‍♀️

And afterward, I wasn’t the same.

The relationship introduced me to someone I hadn’t met before:

MYSELF under those conditions.

Sometimes I liked her.

Sometimes I wanted to shake her by the shoulders.

Eventually I befriended most of them.

Even the super embarrassing ones.

Well...Mostly.

Maybe that’s the better question to ask about relationships.

Not:
Is this my person?

But:
Who are we becoming together?

Because chemistry doesn’t care how spectacular the initial reaction is.

Some reactions produce enormous heat and light and then immediately fall apart.

Very dramatic.
Very romantic.
Terrible shelf life.

Other bonds are quieter.

They hold.

Intensity and stability are not the same property.

So these days I’d rather think of myself as xenon.

A noble gas.

Complete outer shell.
Floating around peacefully.

No vacancies. Thank you.

Noble gases are famously reluctant to bond.

But even xenon will do it under sufficiently unusual conditions.

I find this comforting.

Not:
Complete me.

More:
I was already complete.

So were you.

But something happens when we meet.

Maybe it lasts.
Maybe it doesn’t.

Maybe we create table salt.
Maybe we create an explosion.

Nature offers no guarantees.

But after the reaction, neither of us is quite what stood before.

Maybe that’s what relationship is.

Not two incomplete halves becoming whole.

Two already existing worlds colliding
...
and discovering what else they are capable of becoming.

text:
AT WHAT PRICE — AND FOR WHOM?

I am not denying that Tesla, Starlink, SpaceX, Neuralink, AI or humanoid robotics can produce useful technology. That is not my argument.

My question is much simpler:
Who can actually afford to benefit from it?

A technology can be extraordinary and still remain inaccessible to millions of ordinary people.
A worker, a teacher, a single parent, an elderly person, someone struggling to pay for medical care, or someone without a high income does not automatically gain access simply because a billionaire has invented something impressive.

A Tesla is not free. Starlink is not free. Advanced AI services are not universally free. Experimental medical technologies becoming possible does not mean they will automatically become universally accessible. Professional AI tools for video, design, translation, advertising, research and business increasingly require subscriptions, hardware or other paid services.

And this is exactly the contradiction I keep questioning:
we are told technology will create abundance for everyone, while access to much of that technology still depends on money.

Even AI illustrates the problem perfectly. An AI may tell someone exactly how to create a professional video, design, translation, campaign or business project — but if every tool required to actually do it sits behind another subscription, intelligence alone does not remove economic inequality.

The same question applies to Elon Musk’s companies.

It is easy to list Tesla, SpaceX, Starlink, Neuralink, X and Optimus as evidence of positive impact. But technological achievement and service to humanity are not automatically the same thing.

Who owns the infrastructure?
Who sets the price?
Who gets access?
Who is excluded?
And who becomes more powerful as dependence on these systems increases?

Those questions matter just as much as engineering achievements.

And when discussing generosity, we should also be precise. Forbes’ 2026 ranking of America’s 25 biggest lifetime philanthropists specifically notes that Elon Musk did not make its top 25 under its methodology. Other philanthropy rankings use different methods and do credit Musk with billions in charitable giving, so I am not claiming that he has given nothing. 

My point is different: enormous wealth gives enormous capacity to relieve suffering directly, and it is fair to ask how much of that capacity reaches people who can offer nothing profitable in return. 

To me, power is not most impressive when it demonstrates what one person can own, build or control.
Power becomes meaningful when it lifts people who cannot repay you. And this is where my Christian perspective matters.

JESUS encountered a rich young man who had possessions, morality and status. Yet JESUS challenged him at precisely the point where wealth had become more important than surrender and service:

“Sell that thou hast, and give to the poor… and come and follow me.” — Matthew 19:21

The lesson is not that technology or wealth are evil.
The question is who they serve.

CHRIST did not come among humanity displaying wealth from above. HE humbled HIMSELF, served, healed, fed, taught, touched those whom society ignored and gave without first asking whether the recipient could afford HIM.

That is the model by which I judge claims about “helping humanity.”

I do not measure a better future only by faster rockets, smarter AI, humanoid robots or larger corporations.

I also look at whether the sick can receive care.
Whether ordinary families can live with dignity.
Whether technology reaches the poor as well as the wealthy.
Whether people become freer  or increasingly dependent on systems owned by a few.

Innovation is powerful.
Compassion is greater.
And if the future is truly “for everyone,” then someday we need to stop merely saying those words and start asking whether everyone can actually participate in it.

“For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.”  Matthew 6:21

text:
INOX India Ltd

Inox is increasingly moving towards high-value, technology-intensive cryogenic engineering, supported by strong traction in aerospace, semiconductors, LNG, and scientific research.

⏩️ Q1FY27 performance was subdeued with 8.3% YoY revenue growth, EBITDA growth of 1.4% YoY, while PAT remained flat YoY at 61 Cr.

EBITDA margin at 23.5%, remained within the company's guided 21-24% range. 

⏩️Execution challenges are temporary

1️⃣ Q1FY27 performance was marred by logistical issues, as around Rs 32-35 crore of equipment was ready for dispatch but could not be shipped because of sharply higher freight costs and limited shipping availability.

2️⃣ Some customers also deferred deliveries in anticipation of lower freight rates.

⏩️ Order book positioning

✅️Q1 order intake reached a record Rs 532 crore, the highest quarterly order intake in the company's history.

✅️This pushed the order book to a record Rs 1,686 crore as of June 2026, with export orders accounting for more than Rs 1,140 crore.

✅️ INOX India is moving towards higher-value engineering solutions with improving quality of the backlog, increasing exposure to aerospace, semiconductor infrastructure, LNG, cryogenic science, and specialised industrial applications.

⏩️Aerospace: A major growth driver?

INOX India secured orders for eight large 1,500 cubic metre cryogenic storage tanks and six additional tanks from the same global space customer.

The management indicated that cumulative order exposure from this customer has crossed Rs 1,000 crore, with execution spread over one to two years and deliveries extending to FY28.

✅️The recently secured AS9100D certification allows the company to target flight-qualified applications such as propellant tanks used in rockets.

Significant oppotunity given the limited competitive landscape, with only one major competitor, "Chart Industries", in the large cryogenic tank segment.

⏩️Semiconductors and LNG: The new growth avenues.

✅️INOX has received initial orders for storage and transport equipment for semiconductor facilities in Dholera of around Rs 30 crore. Potential customers include Micron, Foxconn, and Tata's semiconductor projects.

The company's high-purity gas infrastructure capabilities, including cryogenic equipment and VJ transfer lines, could provide a competitive advantage.

✅️Lower global LNG prices are improving the economics of LNG as a transition fuel, supporting demand for LNG fuelling infrastructure. 

INOX has won orders from Sabarmati Gas, Ultra Gas, and BPCL and sees RFQs for around 20–25 LNG stations.

⏩️Cryo-scientific & beverage businesses

1️⃣ INOX secured an order from CERN for specialised cryogenic modules and another order from ITER France, reinforcing its position in technically complex applications.

2️⃣ INOX continues to work with global brewers, including Heineken, AB InBev and Molson Coors, which together represent more than 40% of global beer-market volumes. 

The company is increasingly targeting specialised, non-standard kegs, which will offer superior margins compared to standard commodity kegs.

⏩️Capacity expansion supports execution

The new Kandla facility is progressing rapidly, with commercial operations targeted by Dec 26 or Jan 27. 

The facility should provide additional capacity to execute large aerospace & cryogenic orders.

At Savli, both cryogenic & keg shops are now under full production. The keg facility, with a capacity of around 300,000 kegs, is currently operating below full utilisation, management expects utilisation to increase from around 30% to 50-60% by 2026 end.

⏩️Earnings guidance

Management retained its FY27 revenue guidance of 18-20% & EBITDA margin guidance of 21-24%, despite softer Q1.

The near-term revenue trajectory should benefit from the normalisation of international logistics.

⏩️Valuation at 44xFY28 estimated earnings remain premium but reasonable given niche industry Inox is operating in with high entry barriers.

text:
THE ESTSTE AGENT CEASEFIRE

So a proposed ceasefire because two real estate agents are going to try to convince Putin to stop winning a war ?

So naturally the artillery should take a long weekend off ? 
That is obviously nonsense and everyone should just keep hammering away. 
The “open house” protocol
You do not pause a war because two brokers are doing a walk-through. Imagine the listing: “Historic Eurasian landmass, some water damage, motivated seller, as-is.” 
You keep the drones up. Nothing says “price is firm” like continued shelling during the viewing.
Commission only pays if the deal actually closes
Estate agents live on closings, not vibes. 
A courtesy ceasefire is the diplomatic equivalent of “we’ll think about it.” Keep firing. That is how you create urgency. 
“Nice proposal. Shame if something happened to the remaining energy infrastructure while you were in the air.” 
They already know how to stage a property
Kushner and Witkoff have spent careers making dumpsters look like luxury lofts. 
A couple of days of quiet is just staging. 
Real negotiations happen when the windows are still rattling. Keep hammering. Let them write the offer letter with sirens in the background. Authenticity matters.
The “we paused for the inspectors” clause is a trap
Every developer has seen this movie. The other side agrees to a quiet weekend, then uses it to move the goalposts, hide the mold, and claim the foundation was always like that. 
Do not give them the quiet weekend. Keep the pressure on the load-bearing walls. 
Flight path courtesy is not a peace process
“Please don’t shoot while our guys are overhead” is air-traffic control, not statecraft. 
Airlines do this every day. 
The war can wait for two private jets the same way it waits for commercial flights: it doesn’t. Keep hammering. If they wanted a no-fly zone they should have brought better lawyers. 
Precedent is dangerous
Next week some other pair of well-connected New Yorkers will visit and everyone will be expected to stand down and down missiles again. 
Before long the entire front becomes a series of courtesy pauses for whoever has a good real-estate Rolodex. Ridiculous. The guns should not have a social calendar. 
They are not the UN. They are not even the closing attorney.
These are two men whose professional skill set is “make the other guy think the penthouse is a bargain.” Fine. Let them do that while the actual fighting continues. 
If the proposal is good, it will survive a few extra Grad rockets. If it isn’t, a ceasefire just gives everyone time to put on nicer suits and pretend it is.
Zelensky promised no strikes while they are in Russia. Russia promised the same for Kyiv. 
Eleven minutes after wheels-down in Moscow a Ukrainian drone still finds an oil depot because someone in the chain thought “temporary ceasefire for two brokers” was a joke. 
Witkoff’s phone lights up with “productively constructive” texts while air-raid apps on both sides keep pinging. 
Trump issue a rambling statement: “The market remains active.”
The motorcade in Kyiv is planned like they’re showing a $90 million townhouse: tinted glass, one trusted driver, “don’t mention the cracks.” 
A Russian strike still lands close enough that the windows rattle during the handshake photo. Kushner’s first words on camera: “Solid construction.” Zelensky’s face does the thing. The war does not pause for the photo.
Sunday in Kyiv they produce “a proposal.” Everyone smiles for the cameras. No one puts down their weapons because the proposal still has the same unsold units: territory, NATO language, who pays for the rebuild. 
The two brokers fly home talking about “great momentum.” The front line treats it like every other Saturday-to-Sunday. 
That’s the gag: the visit happens, the talking points happen, the photos happen. The hammering does not clock out for two estate agents doing a showing.
Both sides should keep pounding away like Starmer on a Ukrainian rent boy.
If America want a ceasefire they could have had one in 2022.

WARREN THORNTON

text:
Betting College Football tonight? 

Free analysis & insight 
Toledo at Michigan State 

Pat Fitzgerald’s Michigan State debut against Toledo (Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, 8 p.m. ET, Spartan Stadium, FS1) is one of the Spartans’ more realistic wins on a brutal Big Ten schedule. Fitzgerald’s teams have historically played with toughness, accountability, and fewer self-inflicted wounds; that cultural reset plus home Friday-night lights (MSU has been excellent in those openers) gives the Spartans an edge in a game both sides will treat as a measuring stick.

Michigan State holds clearer advantages in returning production and quarterback experience. Redshirt sophomore Alessio Milivojevic started the final four games of 2025 (1,267 yards, 10 TDs, 3 INTs overall) and is the established starter. Transfer RB Cam Edwards (1,240 yards at UConn) plus other portal additions give MSU high returning rushing production (top-5 nationally in some metrics). Toledo, by contrast, ranks near the bottom of FBS in returning production after massive roster turnover (former coach Jason Candle took key pieces to UConn; ESPN previously listed them 130th). Their QB John Alan Richter is a fifth-year player but has only one career start and limited snaps. Both lines and skill groups are heavily rebuilt, but MSU’s mix of returning starters and high-volume transfers is more proven. 
 
Toledo was excellent last year (8-5, 30.8 PPG scored, 13.3 allowed) and added FCS star DE Andrew Zock, but that defense is mostly new and faces a physical, run-oriented Fitzgerald offense that should control tempo. Week 1 growing pains, a night road game, and Fitzgerald’s emphasis on discipline and fundamentals favor the home team keeping this from becoming a high-scoring track meet.

Wizard of Odds Model:
•  MSU win probability: 76%
•  MSU covers -9.5: 51.7%
•  Under 47.5: 55.7%
•  Under 48.5: 59.1%
•  Toledo outright: ~24%
These line up closely with independent models (Dimers ~76% MSU / 29-19). The market (MSU -9.5 to -10.5, total 47.5-48.5) is roughly efficient on the spread; public money has been on MSU while the line has drifted toward Toledo and the total has dropped, indicating sharp lean the other way. 

Best bet with value: MSU -9.5 or
Under 47.5 for total

New-coach Week 1, two heavily reconstructed rosters, Fitzgerald’s defense-first/physical identity, a returning-but-not-elite MSU offense, and Toledo’s first-year starter on the road all point to sloppy execution, longer drives, and fewer explosive plays. The total has already come down from the mid-49s on sharp Under action; our sim still shows modest edge at 47.5. MSU -9.5 is a reasonable play if you want the Spartans side (home, discipline, production edges), but the Under offers cleaner value given the expected script. Michigan State should win a 24-17 or 27-17 type game and start the Fitzgerald era on the right foot @MSU_Football @ToledoFB
